The Pirate Crash mechanic is the defining product at this platform, and it works differently from any slot or table game in the library. A multiplier starts at 1.00× the moment a round begins and rises continuously along a curved trajectory. The player places a bet before the round starts, then watches the multiplier climb. At any point before the curve crashes — an event determined by a provably fair RNG — they can cash out and lock in their winnings at the current multiplier. If they do not cash out before the crash, the bet is lost. The main compromise of the manual cash-out model is that in order to achieve the highest multipliers, a player must hold their nerve through periods of significant uncertainty. Auto-cashout removes that psychological variable: a player sets a target multiplier (for example, 2.00×) and the system cashes out automatically if that figure is reached, regardless of how high the multiplier continues to climb afterward. To verify any round’s outcome independently, follow these steps:
After a round ends, open the game history and locate the round ID.
Note the server seed hash displayed before the round began — the operator commits to this hash before play starts, making the outcome tamper-evident.
After the round, the platform reveals the unhashed server seed. Combine it with your client seed (visible in your account settings).
Run the combined string through an SHA-256 hashing tool of your choice and confirm the output matches the pre-round hash.
Convert the verified hash to the crash point using the publicly documented formula available in the BGaming provably fair specification.
This process confirms that no crash point can be altered after a player has placed a bet, which is the core trust mechanism underpinning every crash game at the site.
